title: Section 176 — Illegal payments in connection with an election

content.overview: Section 176 — Illegal payments in connection with an election. The operative rule is the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Cite the BNS section, not the repealed Indian Penal Code, for conduct governed by the BNS. Illegal payments in connection with an election. Historical concordance: IPC 171H. For conduct governed by the BNS, cite BNS section 176; the IPC reference is historical concordance. Punishment, ingredients and exceptions are only those the section states. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 176. Whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees:

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body: Whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees:

sections.heading: Exceptions and provisos
sections.body: Provided that if any person having incurred any such expenses not exceeding the amount of ten rupees without authority obtains within ten days from the date on which such expenses were incurred the approval in writing of the candidate, he shall be deemed to have incurred such expenses with the authority of the candidate

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 176 is the rule on “Illegal payments in connection with an election”. The section provides that whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees:. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. Whoever without the general or special authority in writing of a candidate incurs or authorises expenses on account of the holding of any public meeting, or upon any advertisement, circular or publication, or in any other way whatsoever for the purpose of promoting or procuring the election of such candidate, shall be punished with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees:

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Exceptions / provisos.
